_comment: Pinned ccusage build. AgentSpend bundles this binary to read the agent CLIs it
has no native parser for. Pinning by the sha256 of the extracted Mach-O rather
than the tarball is deliberate: npm tarballs can be re-packed with identical
contents and a different archive hash, and it is the executable we are about to
sign with a Developer ID and ship, so that is the artifact worth pinning.
Bumping: run ./vendor-ccusage.sh --update <version>, which rewrites the hashes
here after downloading. Review the diff. Never hand-edit a hash to make a build
pass, because that defeats the only check standing between npm and a notarized
release signed with your own certificate.
ccusage is MIT licensed, Copyright (c) 2025 ryoppippi. See vendor/LICENSE-ccusage,
which vendor-ccusage.sh writes next to the binary and build-app.sh ships.
_agentsNote: The 14 agents the sidecar owns. `claude` and `codex` are deliberately absent:
both have native Swift ingestors that are strictly better. Native Claude matches
ccusage per-date at 1.00x while also retaining 32 days of history that ccusage
cannot see (Claude Code prunes old sessions; the store never deletes), and it
costs no extra memory, where `ccusage claude` peaks at 1.2 GB resident. Native
Codex reads the cumulative running total, which matches Codex's own state sqlite
exactly, where ccusage sums per-turn deltas and loses every dropped token_count
event: 18,513,223 against a true 19,206,339 on this corpus, a 3.6% undercount.
ccusage v20.0.20 exposes 16 agent subcommands, not the 18 its README advertises.
